problem: End-to-end RL policies for image-goal navigation generalize poorly and transfer badly to real robots. On the instance-specific ImageNav task (InstanceImageNav: the goal image shows one particular object, taken with a camera independent of the agent), the end-to-end RL baseline reaches only 8.3% SR, and a SOTA ImageNav model (OVRL-v2) gets 0.6% zero-shot and 24.8% after fine-tuning, while overfitting to Train (85.0% SR).
motivation: An image is a natural way to point a home robot at a particular instance, such as 'this bed' when the home has several beds. Doing so needs both instance-level visual disambiguation and exploration. End-to-end methods need huge sample budgets (3.5B steps on 64 GPUs), overfit, and suffer the sim-to-real gap. Modular pipelines have already proven sample-efficient and real-world-robust for ObjectNav. The paper asks how far a purely modular, zero-fine-tuning pipeline of off-the-shelf components can go on InstanceImageNav.
key_idea: Split InstanceImageNav into exploration, goal instance re-identification, goal localization and local navigation. Frontier exploration searches the map. SuperPoint+SuperGlue keypoint matching against the goal image decides whether the goal is in view (by thresholding the summed match confidence), and the matched keypoints that fall inside a Detic instance mask are depth-projected onto the map as the navigation target for an FMM planner.
insight:
Instance navigation needs local, instance-discriminative matching, not category or global-embedding similarity, and the same keypoint matches can serve both detection and localization.
- Global encoders fail at instance Re-ID: ResNet reaches 13.8% SR and CLIP 9.7%, exhausting the step budget in 86% and 92% of episodes.
- ObjectNav-style class-based localization (Detic-ObjectNav) drops SR from 56.1 to 48.8.
- Summed match confidence beats match count (+2.2 SR).
- A Detic instance mask on the goal image beats a static central crop (+3.8 SR).
- With perfect Re-ID and localization, SR rises to 84.5, so frontier exploration plus local navigation caps the system.
- Oracle Re-ID with the predicted localization (49.8 SR) does not beat the full system, because detection and localization share the keypoint matches: low-confidence detections yield poor localization.
- Across 100 failed episodes, Re-ID false negatives cause 41% of failures and false positives from background matches 23%.
- The threshold τ=24.5 chosen by maximal F-measure on train-split image pairs coincides with the empirically best downstream threshold.
method: Exploration: frontier-based exploration (FBE) on a top-down 2D occupancy / free-space / frontier map, built each step by inverse perspective projection of egocentric depth using the agent pose; the agent greedily goes to the nearest frontier, then repeats.

Goal instance Re-ID (Keypoint-Conf): SuperPoint extracts keypoints and 256-d descriptors from the goal image I* and the egocentric image I_t; SuperGlue (a GNN with optimal-transport matching, indoor weights) matches them with per-match confidences C. The goal counts as detected if sum(C) ≥ τ; this runs every step, with no fine-tuning.
Threshold selection: a pairwise dataset from 3% of train-split instances (121 objects, 2270 goal images); τ is chosen to maximize F-measure on the precision-recall curve (τ = 24.5).

Goal localization (Detic-Projected): Detic (open-vocabulary, CLIP-based) segments the goal image; the mask containing the image center with the highest confidence is kept. Matched keypoints inside this mask are mapped to their egocentric correspondences, lifted to 3D with depth, flattened and voxelized into a 2D goal map channel concatenated with the exploration map.

Local navigation: an incremental Fast Marching Method planner (as in Active Neural SLAM / SemExp) on the occupancy map, decoded greedily into discrete actions toward the nearest reachable frontier or goal point.

Implementation: built on the Home-Robot and SemExp codebases; Detic uses the 21K model with a custom vocabulary {chair, sofa, bed, toilet, potted plant, tv monitor}. On the real Stretch robot, pose comes from Hector SLAM and goal images are taken with a phone.

setting.backbone: Off-the-shelf frozen perception: SuperPoint + SuperGlue (indoor/ScanNet weights) for Re-ID, Detic (21K model) for goal-image instance segmentation. Classical policy: frontier-based exploration + FMM planner.
setting.training_data: none (training-free / zero fine-tuning). Only the Re-ID threshold is tuned, on a pairwise image dataset from the train split (121 objects, 2270 goal images).
setting.observation: Goal RGB image (512x512, independent camera); egocentric RGB + depth (640x360, 42° HFOV, RealSense-like, camera at 1.31 m); agent pose (x, y, θ) relative to the start pose
setting.action_space: discrete: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT 30° / STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D-SEM scenes); plus real-world Hello Robot Stretch
setting.privileged: none (agent pose relative to start is part of the task observation; Hector SLAM in the real world)

numbers.extra: Habitat Challenge 2023 ImageNav-track InstanceImageNav episodes (single-floor only), Stretch embodiment, 1000-step budget, 1.0 m success radius; 1K val episodes

privileged: oracle GT instance mask used for goal localization after positive Re-ID

The main text says 'Keypoint-Match produces 0.972 while Keypoint-Conf produces 0.962' (max F-measure), but Supp. B lists 'Keypoint-Match and Keypoint-Conf (0.962 vs. 0.972)' and says F-measure rank order matches downstream performance, so the main-text ordering looks swapped. The val episode set uses the 2023 Habitat Challenge constraint of no multi-floor episodes.
results: On HM3D InstanceImageNav val, Mod-IIN reaches 56.1% SR / 23.3 SPL / 3.1 NE with zero fine-tuning. This is about 7x the end-to-end IIN RL baseline (8.3% SR, trained for 3.5B steps) and 2.3x OVRL-v2 fine-tuned for IIN (24.8% SR, 11.8 SPL, 5.0 NE); zero-shot OVRL-v2-ImageNav gets 0.6%. Deployed on a Hello Robot Stretch in an office and an apartment, it succeeds in 7/8 episodes (88%).
limitations: Detection and localization are memory-less, with no persistent grounding of the goal in memory. Re-ID false negatives (41% of failures) and background-driven false positives (23%) dominate the errors.

Exploration is plain nearest-frontier FBE (the oracle upper bound is only 84.5 SR). Evaluation uses single-floor episodes only, and the goal categories are restricted to six classes (the Detic vocabulary is set to them).
Real-world evaluation is tiny: 8 episodes and 5 goals in 2 environments.
